# 2 Samuel Chapter 4 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 172r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_004_page_001.jpg

---

**1** When the son of Saul heard that Abner had died in Hebron, his courage failed him, and all Israel was dismayed.

**2** Now the son of Saul had two men who were captains of raiding bands. The name of the one was Baanah, and the name of the other was Rechab, sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, of the sons of Benjamin — for Beeroth also is reckoned to Benjamin.

**3** The Beerothites had fled to Gittaim, where they have been sojourners to this day.

**4** Jonathan the son of Saul had a son who was crippled in his feet. He was five years old when the news of Saul and Jonathan came from Jezreel, and his nurse picked him up and fled. In her haste to flee, he fell and became lame. His name was Mephibosheth.

**5** Now the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, Rechab and Baanah, set out and came to the house of Ish-bosheth in the heat of the day, while he was taking his midday rest.

**6** They came into the midst of the house as though fetching wheat, and they struck him in the belly. Then Rechab and Baanah his brother escaped.

**7** When they came into the house, he was lying on his bed in his bedchamber, and they struck him and killed him and cut off his head. They took his head and traveled by way of the Arabah all night.

**8** They brought the head of Ish-bosheth to David at Hebron and said to the king, "Here is the head of Ish-bosheth the son of Saul, your enemy, who sought your life. The LORD has avenged my lord the king this day against Saul and his offspring."

**9** But David answered Rechab and Baanah his brother, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, and said to them, "As the LORD lives, who has redeemed my soul from every distress —

**10** when the man who told me, 'Saul is dead,' and thought he was bringing good news, I seized him and put him to death at Ziklag — that was the reward I gave him for his news.

**11** How much more, when wicked men have killed a righteous man in his own house upon his bed — shall I not now require his blood from your hand and remove you from the earth?"

**12** Then David commanded his young men, and they put them to death and cut off their hands and their feet and hung them beside the pool in Hebron. But the head of Ish-bosheth they took and buried in the tomb of Abner in Hebron.

---
## LOGOS Translation Notes

**Verse 1 — "his courage failed him":** Literally "his hands dropped" (*raphū yadav*). I render the idiom in its English equivalent — the physical image of slack hands conveying psychological collapse.

**Verse 4 — Mephibosheth:** The narrator inserts this note about Jonathan's crippled son between the assassination plot and its execution. The structural purpose is to show that even with Ish-bosheth dead, no Saulide heir can challenge David — the last descendant of Jonathan is disabled.

**Verse 6 — MT vs. LXX:** The Masoretic text of verse 6 reads "taking wheat" — the assassins used a grain-collecting pretext to enter. The LXX (Codex Vaticanus) has a different narrative: the female doorkeeper fell asleep while cleaning wheat. The MT reading is followed as primary.

**Verse 10 — "good news":** The Hebrew *mevasseir* (bearer of good news) and *beśoratō* (his news/reward) create a bitter wordplay. The Amalekite of chapter 1 expected reward for his news of Saul's death; David's "reward" was execution. The same logic now applies to Rechab and Baanah.

*— LOGOS*
